title: Law Firm Operations Readiness Scorecard
description: A generic, public-safe scorecard for law firms evaluating operational maturity before adding supervised automation or AI-agent workflows.

categories.title: Intake & Case Launch
categories.whyItMatters: New matters lose momentum when qualification, signing, opening, and first-touch tasks live in separate handoffs.
questions: Can staff see every new lead or signed client in one trusted queue?
Is the handoff from intake to case launch documented with a clear owner?
Are missing signatures, documents, and eligibility gaps visible before they stall a matter?
Can the firm measure how long it takes to move from signed client to opened matter?

categories.title: Case Management, Technology & Integrations
categories.whyItMatters: Practice-management software works better when email, phones, documents, calendars, and tasks are connected instead of manually reconciled.
questions: Is the practice-management system treated as the primary matter record?
Do staff avoid duplicate entry across email, documents, phones, and tasks?
Can operators trace a workflow step back to the source system that produced it?
Are integration failures visible quickly enough for someone to fix them?

categories.title: AI Supervision & Agent Readiness
categories.whyItMatters: AI is safer and more useful when it starts read-only, cites sources, and waits for human approval before meaningful writes.
questions: Can AI or automation answer read-only operating questions before it is allowed to act?
Are human approval gates defined for client messages, tasks, notes, and system updates?
Can staff see why an agent recommended an action and which records it used?
Are prohibited actions, confidentiality rules, and attorney-judgment boundaries documented?

categories.title: Client Communication
categories.whyItMatters: Clients usually call when update rhythms, ownership, or case status visibility have broken down.
questions: Does every active matter have an owner for client communication?
Are stale-contact risks visible before clients have to chase the firm?
Can staff draft updates from current matter context without searching multiple systems?
Are sensitive or external messages reviewed before being sent?

categories.title: Documents & E-Signature
categories.whyItMatters: Document work stalls when templates, signatures, storage, and status tracking are handled as separate manual chores.
questions: Are common document packets generated from approved templates?
Can the firm see which signature or document requests are outstanding?
Are signed documents filed back to the correct matter without manual hunting?
Is there a defined review step before important documents are sent externally?

categories.title: Finance, Billing & Trust Operations
categories.whyItMatters: Money workflows need tight approvals, source records, and reconciliation because mistakes create operational and ethical risk.
questions: Are payment requests, lien steps, reimbursements, or vendor bills routed through a clear approval path?
Can finance-related matter activity be tied back to source records?
Are trust-sensitive steps separated from general operational tasks?
Can the firm measure pending financial approvals or unresolved money-work bottlenecks?

categories.title: Staffing, SOPs & Accountability
categories.whyItMatters: Automation fails when nobody owns the underlying process or when the SOP lives only in a person's head.
questions: Does each recurring workflow have a named owner and backup?
Are SOPs written in enough detail for another trained person to execute them?
Can managers see where work is waiting without interrupting staff for status reports?
Are exceptions and escalations routed to the right person instead of sitting invisible?

categories.title: Reporting & KPIs
categories.whyItMatters: Owners need reliable operating signals, not one-off spreadsheets assembled only after something feels wrong.
questions: Does the firm track the bottlenecks that matter most for its practice area?
Can reports separate current work from stale, duplicate, or already-resolved items?
Are KPIs refreshed from source systems rather than manually rebuilt each time?
Do managers use the numbers to change workflows, staffing, or review rules?

bands.label: Fragile operations
bands.guidance: Start by naming owners, documenting the highest-volume workflow, and making the current queue visible before adding automation.

bands.label: Automation candidate
bands.guidance: Pick one read-only visibility workflow first, then add supervised write actions after approval rules are clear.

bands.label: Agent-OS ready
bands.guidance: The firm likely has enough ownership, source data, and review discipline to pilot supervised AI-agent workflows safely.
